speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by understanding your history: you mentioned gait and limb ataxia. Can you describe how these symptoms have progressed over time and if there are any other neurological issues you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunken" appearance is a concerning sign of cerebellar dysfunction. Do you experience any slurred speech (dysarthria), double vision, or significant nausea/dizziness alongside the clumsiness? Also, do you have any history of trauma, heavy alcohol use, or autoimmune diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast; REQUEST TEST: Anti-MOG and anti-GQ1b antibodies.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, we must urgently rule out an autoimmune demyelinating event or paraneoplastic syndrome, but please note that natalizumab carries a risk of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which typically presents with cognitive changes and motor weakness rather than isolated ataxia. Please also tell me if you have recently had a flu-like illness or fever.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial and coronal slices.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
